_about: Three critical frames on cultural institutions, shown on the records they apply to as critiques of kind 'theory'. A frame is either a paraphrase ('summary', shown with no author or citation by the editor's decision; the works it rests on are listed under 'rests_on' for the editor only) or a list of short verbatim 'quotes', each with its author, source and url, all shown on the page. tools/attach_critiques.py writes them; re-running replaces them.

frames.target: Museums of modern and contemporary art, biennials and festivals
frames.summary: A museum keeps what has fallen out of use, and that store is what lets anyone call a new work new: the new is measured against what the collection already holds. Artists who attack the museum still want to be kept by it, because outside the archive a work is forgotten. Lately the store has turned into a stage. Shows are run as events, each curator overturns the last one's story, and the internet has taken over the job of remembering, so the museum records its events instead of preserving things. Inside an installation the visitor stands on the artist's ground, under the artist's rules, and is the one being watched.
frames.impact: Read a museum's event calendar and curatorial turnover against what it actually keeps, conserves and pays for.
rests_on: Entering the Flow: Museum between Archive and Gesamtkunstwerk, e-flux journal 50 (2013)

frames.strategy: The gift that follows the taking
frames.target: Institutions funded by donors whose money carries a flag
frames.summary: Giving comes after taking: the money has to be made before it can be given away, and the giving is then told as gratitude and repair. The founder who breaks unions and then endows libraries, the speculator who destabilises an economy in the morning and funds civil society in the afternoon, are one hand hurting and healing. Culture sits inside that portfolio, so a named wing repairs the donor's standing more surely than it repairs any damage. The same move sells the ethical cup of coffee: buy the right thing and the absolution is included in the price. Charity treats the symptom and so keeps the illness going. Large art events that speak in anti-capitalist language are ventures of the capital they describe, and the first honest act may be to decline the invitation to take part.
frames.impact: Where a flag names an industry, ask what the gift was repairing, and for whom.
rests_on: Nobody has to be vile, London Review of Books 28/7 (2006)
First as Tragedy, Then as Farce (2009), the RSA lecture of the same year

frames.target: Biennials, festivals and touring exhibitions, and the cities that host them

quotes.text: Art must not be anodyne, culture cannot be decorative. [Artists] should be feared by the powerful in our society; if you are not, you are not doing your job properly.
quotes.author: Yanis Varoufakis
quotes.source: keynote closing the 6th Moscow Biennale, 1 October 2015, as reported by The Art Newspaper, 3 October 2015

quotes.text: Documenta took a great deal more from Athens—from both its private and public sector—than it gave. […] When Documenta comes here and talks about neoliberalism with no mention of Deutsche Bank, Société Générale, the awful Troika process, the Eurogroup, etc., it is choosing to be irrelevant.
quotes.author: Yanis Varoufakis
quotes.source: ‘We Come Bearing Gifts’, in conversation with iLiana Fokianaki on documenta 14 Athens, art-agenda / e-flux criticism, 7 June 2017

frames.impact: Read a festival's balance with its host city, and its critique against its sponsor list.
